reasoning_traces.think:
FactorMiner addresses three core challenges in automated factor discovery: combinatorial search complexity, poor knowledge retention, and interpretability. The Ralph Loop mitigates combinatorial explosion by sequentially generating and evaluating candidate factors rather than exploring all combinations. Modular skill architecture ensures reuse of validated components, preventing repeated trial-and-error. Experience memory stores successful patterns and forbidden regions, allowing the system to learn from prior sessions and avoid redundancy. As the factor library expands, the 'Correlation Red Sea' problem emerges—where increasing similarity among signals degrades signal quality. FactorMiner counters this by enforcing strict validation protocols and using IC-weighted factor combinations to maintain diversity. The system's design supports scalability through structured memory and modular composition, ensuring that knowledge accumulates effectively across sessions.
